description: I’m passionate about technology, innovation, science, and problem solving, and I’m looking to build a collaborative team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We’re looking for skills in Coding, Software, Web Development, Graphic Design, Science, Data Analysis, Data Visualization, AI/ML, and Data Management. Creativity, teamwork, and enthusiasm matter most. Let’s build something amazing together!
summary:
AstroVital AI is a space health and mission wellness platform that helps astronauts understand their own health when Earth can’t answer. On long Moon and Mars missions, communication can be delayed or lost, while heart, sleep, radiation and exercise signals sit in separate tools.
We built one dashboard covering four health domains. It learns each astronaut’s personal baseline using transparent statistics (median/MAD, robust z-score, EWMA and CUSUM) and flags lasting drift with a risk score, a confidence level and the factors behind every alert. Results appear on an interactive digital twin, a rule-based Copilot that explains alerts without inventing anything, and an offline-first Blackout Mode that keeps working with no connection.
We tested the method on real NASA OSD-575 Inspiration4 data (4 astronauts, 9 biomarkers). Every value carries a source label, and missing data is never shown as healthy. This matters because crews must act safely and independently far from Earth. AstroVital AI is decision support, not diagnosis.
details:
AstroVital AI is an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring platform designed for long-duration space missions. It learns individual health baselines, monitors four domains (Cardiovascular, Brain & Sleep, Radiation, and Muscle & Bone), and detects unusual health patterns using statistical algorithms. It visualizes health conditions through an interactive 2D astronaut digital twin, provides explainable alerts through a Health Copilot, and supports offline operation through Blackout Mode.

It enables personalized health monitoring, early detection of unusual health trends, explainable health alerts, and intuitive visualization. Its offline functionality allows astronauts to access locally stored health information and maintain health records during communication disruptions with Earth.

AstroVital AI aims to improve astronaut health awareness and support autonomous health decision-making during Moon and Mars missions. It envisions more reliable health monitoring in environments where immediate medical assistance and continuous communication with Earth may be unavailable.

Tools:

Language: JavaScript

Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS

Backend: Node.js, Express.js

Visualization: Recharts, Framer Motion, Inline SVG

Data Storage: IndexedDB, optional Supabase

Offline Support: Vite PWA and Service Workers

Deployment: Vercel

Algorithms: Median, MAD, Robust Z-score, EWMA, and CUSUM

Research Data: NASA Open Science Dataset OSD-575.

Its main innovation is personalized health monitoring through individual baselines rather than generic population averages. It combines multi-signal trend detection, an interactive astronaut digital twin, explainable AI alerts, and offline Blackout Mode into one platform designed specifically for deep-space missions.

We considered communication delays, individual physiological differences, multiple health domains, gradual health changes, data quality, scientific reliability, offline functionality, user experience, and medical safety. We also ensured that NASA research, measured, self-reported, and simulated data are clearly distinguished.
